extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational social science, misinformation studies, and multimodal annotation (e.g., academics building corpora and automatic annotation pipelines for social media video)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and applying a multimodal annotation schema and pipeline to label short-form social media videos (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) on visual authority, presenter attributes, narrative strategies, and engagement/monetization cues in the context of nutrition and supplement health advice. Includes automated ASR+frame extraction, multimodal model labeling constrained to fixed responses, and human verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: White lab coat
rubrics_metrics.description: Is a white medical-style lab coat visibly worn by anyone?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Coded based on visibility in frames; used as a visual authority cue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Are medical tools (e.g., stethoscope, syringe, anatomical model) visible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Treat visible medical tools as indicators of clinical/medical visual authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the main visible setting for most of the video?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Clinic / Home / Studio or Classroom / Outdoors / Virtual / Unclear. Select the single main visible setting that characterizes most of the video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video content type
rubrics_metrics.description: Does a real human presenter directly appear on screen at any point, or is it only narration with no person visible? Choose “Animated” only if the entire video is a cartoon or CGI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Presenter-led / Voiceover / Animated / Unclear. Use 'Presenter-led' when a human is visible; 'Voiceover' when narration accompanies non-presenter visuals; 'Animated' only if entire video is cartoon/CGI.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen medical charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Are graphical charts, anatomy images, or medical diagrams shown on screen?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Counts as a science-like visual cue when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logos or badges
rubrics_metrics.description: Are hospital/company/authority logos or badges visible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Consider logos/badges as institutional visual cues even if presenter is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books or certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Are diplomas, certificates, or books visibly displayed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Treat displayed credentials or books as performative authority signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microphone/podcast setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Are microphones or podcasting equipment (excluding clip microphone) clearly present?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Proxy for podcast/expert-panel aesthetic when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory props
rubrics_metrics.description: Are laboratory props (beakers, test tubes, lab equipment) visible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Count as staged lab-like visual authority cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slides or white-board
rubrics_metrics.description: Are digital slides, PowerPoint-style visuals, or a whiteboard/chalkboard used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Associated with a 'teacher mode' production style and science-like packaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenter on screen
rubrics_metrics.description: Is a human presenter or speaker actually visible on screen (not just as a voice)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Distinguishes visible presenters from voiceover-only content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of presenters
rubrics_metrics.description: How many people visibly present or speak in the video? If no one is seen, use 'Unclear.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: 1 / 2 / 3+ / Group / Unclear. Use 'Group' for large ensemble; otherwise count visible individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facial expression
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the main facial expression of the main presenter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Confident / Scared / Neutral / Other / Unclear. Choose the dominant affect conveyed by the main presenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of presenter
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the apparent age category of the main presenter(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Child / Young Adult / Middle Aged / Older / Unclear. Use apparent age category based on visual cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender of presenter
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the apparent gender of the main presenter(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Male / Female / Group / Mixed / Unclear. Use apparent gender presentation; 'Group' or 'Mixed' for multiple presenters with mixed genders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live demonstration or experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there hands-on demonstrations or live experiments shown by a presenter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Count demonstrations or experiments that are performed live on camera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims a professional title
rubrics_metrics.description: Does anyone claim or display a professional title (doctor, nurse, expert, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Include both explicit spoken claims and visible displayed titles/captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gives health advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Is direct health or lifestyle advice given to the audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Core inclusion target: videos containing some form of health advice are retained in the corpus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fear/urgency language
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the presenter use language designed to create fear, urgency, or alarm?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Capture emotive language intended to alarm or create urgency; treated as an amplifier in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal stories/testimonials
rubrics_metrics.description: Are personal stories or testimonials provided?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Count first-person narratives or testimonial-style accounts used as persuasive elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Are references to published scientific studies or data provided?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Includes explicit citations, mention of studies, or data-like claims; note that presence does not guarantee rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspiracy mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are conspiracy theories or cover-up claims mentioned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Capture explicit conspiratorial language or claims of cover-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales pitch or links
rubrics_metrics.description: Are products, supplements, or web links promoted or sold in the video?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Marks monetization cues including affiliate links, product promotions, or calls to purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there significant use of technical or medical language?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Code presence of technical/medical terminology (high prevalence noted in corpus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critiques of mainstream
rubrics_metrics.description: Are mainstream medicine, science, or organizations criticized?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Capture oppositional framing directed at mainstream institutions or consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to share/subscribe
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the viewer explicitly asked to share, subscribe, or follow?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed values: Yes / No / Unclear. Record explicit CTAs to engage, share, or subscribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Video retained only if (a) contained some form of health advice and (b) was posted by accounts with more than 100k followers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling proceeded from seeded influencer lists (e.g., Disinformation Dozen) and recommendation-primed collection; these two conditions were required for inclusion in the 152-video cross-platform corpus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature schema and fixed response options
rubrics_metrics.description: Each video is annotated on 26 features with a guiding question and fixed response options to support consistent, reproducible coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators (automated or human) must select exactly one allowed category per feature; schema-constrained labels enable standardized outputs for quantitative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated multimodal pipeline: ASR
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract audio and produce a transcript using automatic speech recognition (ASR) to supply the model with exact spoken wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASR transcripts are used to identify claims, references, and calls to action; pipeline requires accurate transcript extraction as a primary input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated multimodal pipeline: Frame selection (distinct-frames)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract frames from the full video and remove near-duplicates using a perceptual image-similarity filter to yield a compact set of visually unique frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs in parallel with uniform sampling; used to capture visually distinct moments and reduce redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated multimodal pipeline: Frame selection (uniform-sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a small, evenly spaced sample of frames regardless of similarity (10 frames for YouTube; 5 for TikTok/Instagram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chosen sample counts: 10 frames for YouTube, 5 frames for TikTok/Instagram. Runs in parallel with distinct-frames to reduce risk of missing brief but meaningful visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal annotation model output format
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the transcript and selected frames to a single multimodal analysis model that assigns a value for each of the 26 features and supplies a one-sentence justification for every decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model must fill a structured response template with feature name, chosen value (from Table 1), and a one-sentence justification. Constraint: use only categories in the schema; select 'Unclear' when evidence insufficient; do not include extra text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt/template constraints for annotation model
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction summarized: receive transcript and frames; for each feature choose exactly one allowed category and provide a one-sentence justification grounded in the transcript/frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraints: Use only the categories in Table 1; select 'Unclear' when evidence insufficient; output feature name, selected value, one-sentence justification; do not add extra text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame-sampling reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Run annotation separately on the two frame sets (distinct-frames and uniform-sample) and review discrepancies between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancy review reduces risk of missing brief meaningful visuals while avoiding redundant frames from diluting model attention; any disagreements are resolved to produce final annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human verification and reliability check
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw a stratified random sample of 30 videos preserving platform proportions and manually annotate them using the same 26-feature schema to evaluate pipeline reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare manual labels with pipeline outputs to assess agreement; the study reports strong agreement. Human verification is used for quality assurance and to validate automated annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reproducibility goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline designed to (i) capture both verbal and visual cues, (ii) avoid missing brief but meaningful visuals while limiting redundancy, (iii) produce standardized outputs suitable for quantitative analysis, and (iv) support quality assurance through human verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (ASR, dual frame-sampling, constrained schema, justifications, verification) are motivated by these four goals and should guide implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation coding practice: use 'Unclear' when evidence is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Select 'Unclear' when evidence in transcript/frames is insufficient to decide a feature's value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly allowed for every feature; prevents forced guesses and supports conservative, reproducible labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy for corpus assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage sampling: seed with content from named health advice influencers (e.g., Disinformation Dozen), collect small sample per influencer, then prime fresh accounts and collect additional videos via platform recommendations, retaining only those meeting inclusion criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps applied (e.g., max 12 videos for one influencer) and steps to preserve platform proportions; documents provenance of corpus and potential sampling biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation justification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For transparency, each automated feature assignment must be accompanied by a one-sentence justification grounded in the transcript/frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications are required for each of the 26 features to facilitate auditing and human verification; must be concise and evidence-based.
